This patch prepares the kernel to support putting all kinds of kfunc BTF
ID sets in the struct btf itself. The various kernel subsystems will
make register_btf_kfunc_id_set call in the initcalls (for built-in code
and modules).
The 'hook' is one of the many program types
column2: e.g. XDP and TC/SCHED_CLS

column1: STRUCT_OPS
column2: and 'types' are check (allowed or not)

column1: and ret_null (with PTR_TO_BTF_ID_OR_NULL return type).
A maximum of BTF_KFUNC_SET_MAX_CNT (32) kfunc BTF IDs are permitted in a
set of certain hook and type for vmlinux sets
column2: since they are allocated

column1: on demand
column2: and otherwise set as NULL. Module sets can only be registered

column1: once per hook and type
column2: hence they are directly assigned.

column1: A new btf_kfunc_id_set_contains function is exposed for use in verifier
this new method is faster than the existing list searching method
column2: and

column1: is also automatic. It also lets other code not care whether the set is
unallocated or not.
Note that module code can only do single register_btf_kfunc_id_set call
per hook. This is why sorting is only done for in-kernel vmlinux sets
because there might be multiple sets for the same hook and type that
must be concatenated
column2: hence sorting them is required to ensure bsearch

column1: in btf_id_set_contains continues to work correctly.
Next commit will update the kernel users to make use of this
infrastructure.
Finally
column2: add __maybe_unused annotation for BTF ID macros for the

column1: !CONFIG_DEBUG_INFO_BTF case
column2: so that they don't produce warnings during

column1: build time.
The previous patch is also needed to provide synchronization against
initialization for module BTF's kfunc_set_tab introduced here
column2: as

column1: described below:
The kfunc_set_tab pointer in struct btf is write-once (if we consider
the registration phase (comprised of multiple register_btf_kfunc_id_set
calls) as a single operation). In this sense
column2: once it has been fully

column1: prepared
column2: it isn't modified
column3: only used for lookup (from the verifier

column1: context).
For btf_vmlinux
column2: it is initialized fully during the do_initcalls phase

column1: which happens fairly early in the boot process
column2: before any processes are

column1: present. This also eliminates the possibility of bpf_check being called
at that point
column2: thus relieving us of ensuring any synchronization between

column1: the registration and lookup function (btf_kfunc_id_set_contains).
However
column2: the case for module BTF is a bit tricky. The BTF is parsed

column1: prepared
column2: and published from the MODULE_STATE_COMING notifier callback.

column1: After this
column2: the module initcalls are invoked

column1: function will be called to populate the kfunc_set_tab for module BTF.
At this point
column2: BTF may be available to userspace while its corresponding

column1: module is still intializing. A BTF fd can then be passed to verifier
using bpf syscall (e.g. for kfunc call insn).
Hence
column2: there is a race window where verifier may concurrently try to

column1: lookup the kfunc_set_tab. To prevent this race
column2: we must ensure the

column1: operations are serialized
column2: or waiting for the __init functions to

column1: complete.
In the earlier registration API
column2: this race was alleviated as verifier

column1: bpf_check_mod_kfunc_call didn't find the kfunc BTF ID until it was added
by the registration function (called usually at the end of module __init
function after all module resources have been initialized). If the
verifier made the check_kfunc_call before kfunc BTF ID was added to the
list
column2: it would fail verification (saying call isn't allowed). The

column1: access to list was protected using a mutex.
Now
column2: it would still fail verification

column1: (returning ENXIO due to the failed btf_try_get_module call in
add_kfunc_call)
column2: because if the __init call is in progress the module

column1: will be in the middle of MODULE_STATE_COMING -> MODULE_STATE_LIVE

column2: and the BTF_MODULE_LIVE flag for btf_module instance will

column1: not be set
column2: so the btf_try_get_module call will fail.
